description: An Android app that encourages more mindful screen-time habits through usage statistics, reminders, and guided breathing exercises.

idea.heading: Awareness, not restriction.
idea.paragraph1: What if a screen-time application helped people recognize their habits instead of simply blocking access?
idea.paragraph2: Stillia helps users become more aware of their screen time without restricting their phone usage. Users choose how long a session should last and receive two short vibrations two minutes before it ends. When the session ends, a 30-second animation with vibrations encourages users to slow down and focus on their pulse. Afterwards, users can choose whether or not to continue with a guided breathing exercise (breathwork).
idea.technology: Android · Kotlin · UX Design · Requirements Engineering
idea.imageAlt: Stillia grounding experience with a heartbeat-inspired animation

meta.originValue: Individual university B-level project in Informatics
meta.collaborationValue: Developed in collaboration with a startup company
meta.roleValue: Sole developer · Research · UX · Requirements · Testing

challenge.heading: - From automatic scrolling to conscious choices.
challenge.p1: Smartphones make it easy to move between social media, entertainment and other applications without noticing how much time has passed. What begins as a short interaction can become a much longer session than originally intended.
challenge.p2: Many existing digital wellbeing tools focus on monitoring usage, enforcing limits or blocking applications. Stillia explores whether a less restrictive approach can support awareness while allowing users to remain in control.
challenge.p3: The central design challenge was to create a reminder that users would notice without making the experience stressful, judgmental or unnecessarily disruptive.

research.heading: - Understanding habits before designing solutions.
research.p1: I conducted a user survey with 40 respondents to explore screen-time habits, interest in the concept and preferences for different types of reminders.
research.p2: The results suggested that unplanned screen use was a familiar problem for many participants and that there was initial interest in a gentler approach.
research.p3: Social media and short-form videos were the activities most often associated with using a phone longer than intended.
research.p4: Open-ended responses provided additional perspectives. Participants emphasized simplicity, flexible reminders and the importance of avoiding interruptions during intentional or work-related phone use.
research.p5: Suggestions also included saving a preferred session duration and providing clearer information about usage patterns across applications and time periods.
research.p6: These findings helped me identify opportunities for the product design. They represent initial preferences and stated interest, rather than evidence of long-term behavioural change.

competitors.heading: - Exploring what already exists.
competitors.p1: Before developing the solution, I examined existing approaches to digital wellbeing, screen-time management and mindfulness.
competitors.p2: My research included tools such as Android Digital Wellbeing, Apple Screen Time, Forest, One Sec and Opal, alongside mindfulness applications including Calm, Headspace and The Breathing App.
competitors.p3: This comparison helped me shape the product direction: focusing on awareness and personal choice rather than making blocking or gamification the central interaction.

requirements.heading: - Turning research into product decisions.
requirements.p1: I created and managed a structured list of 58 numbered requirements. They covered the entire experience, including onboarding, session management, heartbeat-inspired signals, the pause feature, breathing exercises and daily screen-time goals.
requirements.p2: I documented requirements with priorities and implementation statuses to support development planning and follow-up.
requirements.p3: These examples illustrate how research findings and product requirements informed my design decisions. I continued refining some features after completing the university project.

experience.heading: - A pause at the right moment.
experience.p1: Before using a selected application, users can choose how long they intend to spend there. Stillia suggests durations based on the application category while leaving the final decision to the user.
experience.p2: This creates an opportunity to make a conscious decision before beginning an activity that might otherwise continue automatically.
experience.p3: When the selected session time ends, Stillia activates a pause sequence designed to shift attention away from the screen and toward the body.
experience.p4: Rather than immediately blocking access, the experience introduces a gradual transition using animation and haptic feedback.
experience.p5: The sequence begins with a pulsing animation accompanied by vibrations inspired by a heartbeat. The rhythm is based on a resting heart rate entered by the user.
experience.p6: Users can optionally begin a guided breathing exercise by holding their thumb against the centre of the animation.
experience.p7: The exercise includes four levels with repeated cycles of inhaling, holding, exhaling and holding again. The intervals increase from two to four, six and eight seconds across the levels.
experience.p8: The entire breathing exercise takes almost eight minutes. The video shows a shortened version before moving to the final stage, where the screen gradually fades to black.
experience.p9: The breathing interaction is optional and can be interrupted. The goal is to encourage a conscious pause rather than force the user to stop using their phone.

application.heading: - Designed around personal control.
application.p1: Stillia brings together session management, the pause feature, personal settings and screen-time statistics in an Android app.
application.p2: Users can adjust preferences and configure how they interact with the application. Personal control was an important consideration throughout my design process.

statistics.heading: - Making screen-time patterns easier to understand.
statistics.p1: In addition to individual sessions, Stillia provides an overview of screen-time habits. The home screen shows daily usage in relation to a personal goal and breaks down activity by category.
statistics.p2: Weekly and monthly statistics allow users to explore usage over time, while session history provides a record of previous interactions.

development.heading: - Iterating through implementation and evaluation.
development.p1: I developed the Android application using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, with supporting backend functionality built using Java and Spring Boot.
development.p2: Throughout the project, I worked with interface design, application logic, Android platform functionality and iterative testing.
development.p3: I used planned functional tests, user evaluations and ad hoc testing to investigate how the application behaved in different situations.
development.p4: During ad hoc testing, I identified an issue where picture-in-picture video could continue playing during the pause sequence. The issue was documented as fixed in the original test log.
development.p5: Another recorded issue concerned permission information remaining visible after the required permission had been granted. This was still marked as open in the original test log.
development.p6: These findings demonstrated the importance of testing Android system interactions, particularly for an application designed to work alongside other apps.
development.p7: The evaluations provided feedback on the prototype's functionality and usability. They did not establish whether Stillia produces sustained reductions in screen time.

context.heading: - From a university project to Stillia.
context.p1: Stillia originated as an individual university B-level project in Informatics, carried out in collaboration with a startup company.
context.p2: I was solely responsible for the project's user research, competitor analysis, requirements engineering, UX design, Android development and testing.
context.p3: Following the university project, I continued developing and refining the application, including its visual identity, statistics, interface consistency and demo functionality.
context.p4: This case study presents my work across the complete product development process, from initial research and planning to implementation, evaluation and iteration.

reflection.heading: - Building around the user, not just the technology.
reflection.p1: Stillia gave me the opportunity to take responsibility for an entire product development process, from understanding a problem and evaluating existing solutions to defining requirements, designing interactions, implementing functionality and testing the result.
reflection.p2: One of the most interesting challenges was finding a balance between helpful feedback and respect for the user’s autonomy. A reminder needs to be noticeable to encourage awareness, but should not be so disruptive that it creates frustration.
reflection.p3: Working independently also required me to prioritize features, make technical and design decisions and evaluate the results throughout development.
reflection.p4: The project strengthened my interest in combining technical development with user experience, research, requirements engineering and thoughtful product decisions.

longer.finding: People often spend longer in apps than they intend.
longer.decision: Introduce intentional sessions where users choose a duration before starting.

subtle.finding: Users expressed interest in subtle, non-intrusive feedback.
subtle.decision: Explore heartbeat-inspired vibration and animation instead of relying only on conventional alerts.

control.finding: Users wanted flexibility and control over their experience.
control.decision: Support personal settings, selected applications and user-controlled sessions.

insights.finding: Users wanted to better understand their screen-time habits.
insights.decision: Present daily usage, category breakdowns and weekly and monthly statistics.
